# Public repo contribution inflow

Plan: `open-source-release-2026-09-29` (P-011). Decisions it rests on: D-003 (ELv2), D-004 (two repos, CLA not DCO, append-only public history), D-016 (public repo name), D-017 (public CI scope).

## The model in one paragraph

`Papercusp/papercup` (private) is the **only** source of truth. `Papercusp/papercusp-app` (public, ELv2) is an **append-only export**: every public commit is produced by `node scripts/source-preview.mjs push --target public --confirm`, which re-exports a public-safe cut, runs the gate (secrets, identity, licence notices), and appends one commit on top of public `main` without `--force`. Nothing is ever merged directly on the public repo — a direct merge would be overwritten by the next export's tree and would bypass the gate. ⚠ `Papercusp/papercusp` is NOT the public repo: it is the private `libs/papercusp` library (D-016); the export refuses to target it.

## What the export ships for contributors

From `scripts/public-release/`, copied verbatim by the public target (`PUBLIC_COMMUNITY_FILES`): `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `CLA.md`, `.github/workflows/cla.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

- **`ci.yml`** — plain `pull_request` with `contents: read`: `npm ci` + `npm run lint:tsc`, the steps measured green on a clean export copy. The test suite is not yet in the export (D-017, WI-10004090).
- **`cla.yml`** — CLA Assistant on `pull_request_target` (it needs a write token to comment and record signatures on the `cla-signatures` branch, never `main`). It must **never check out PR code**. Both workflow properties are pinned by `packages/operator-core/lib/source-preview-public.test.ts`.
- **`CLA.md`** — individual CLA: copyright + patent licence including relicensing beyond ELv2; contributor keeps copyright.

## Flow for an outside pull request

1. **Triage on the public repo.** Anything larger than a small fix should have had an issue first (CONTRIBUTING.md asks for this); if not, ask for one before reviewing in depth.
2. **CLA check.** The CLA status check must be green. No CLA → no port. Documentation typo fixes are exempt (CONTRIBUTING.md). The CLA is required because under ELv2 an inbound=outbound contribution would bind us by ELv2's own hosted-service limit (D-004 §2).
3. **Review the change as code.** Same bar as internal work: tests in the project's framework, typecheck, no dependency whose licence conflicts with ELv2 (`scripts/check-licenses.mjs` enforces this on the export).
4. **Port it into the private tree.** Apply the PR diff to the canonical `staging` tree (`https://github.com/Papercusp/papercusp-app/pull/<N>.diff`; paths are identical because the export preserves layout). Exceptions: the public-only files above live under `scripts/public-release/`, and `NOTICE` / `README.md` / `MANIFEST.json` / `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` are GENERATED — port such a change into `scripts/source-preview.mjs` / `scripts/check-licenses.mjs`. Register a work-item `Port public PR #<N>: <title>` with the PR URL and the contributor's `Name <email>` (from the PR commits). Run the full suite for the area (`npm run test:affected -- --changed-paths=…`) — the contributor could not; report any failure on the PR. git-sync commits it; the private commit will NOT carry the contributor's identity, which is why step 6 exists.
5. **Let it reach green `main`.** The public export defaults to `--ref main`, so the port ships only once the green checkpoint has promoted it.
6. **Ship it back out with credit.** `node scripts/source-preview.mjs push --target public --confirm --co-author "Name <email>"` (repeat `--co-author` per contributor) appends a public commit with one `Co-authored-by:` trailer each. A malformed value is refused before any export work (`coAuthorTrailers`, pinned by `packages/operator-core/lib/source-preview-sync.test.ts`).
7. **Close the PR** with a comment linking the public commit (`pushedCommit` in the push output). Close the port work-item citing the same commit.

If a contribution cannot be accepted (scope, licence, quality), close the PR with the reason; never leave it silently open.

## Changes that must not flow out

The export's selection (shared with the installer) already drops the closed set from D-004 §3 and anything the gate flags. A PR that edits a path absent from the public cut is either against a stale fork or touching something we do not publish — reject with an explanation rather than porting.

## Issue tracker policy

- **Public issues live on `Papercusp/papercusp-app`.** Maintainers mirror anything actionable into the private work-item ledger (`work_items:create`, issue URL in the body) and link back; the public issue is closed when the fix ships in an export, citing the public commit.
- **Private-only work stays private.** Internal work-items are not mirrored out.
- **Security reports never go in public issues.** SECURITY.md routes reporters to the private channel; handle those as private work-items and ship the fix before disclosure.
- Labels on the public repo are the minimum set: `bug`, `enhancement`, `question`, `good first issue`, `needs-cla`.

## Why not merge on GitHub

Merging on the public repo would (a) create public history the next append-only export does not descend from, so `pushSnapshot` would refuse with `public main moved during the push`, and (b) publish code that never passed the private test suite or the export gate. Porting keeps one source of truth and one gate.
